title: How exercise could boost your exam grades
titleChinese: 为什么运动能助你的考试成绩 “一臂之力”
paragraphs: Has exam season got you hitting the books instead of the gym? Study is important, but if you're not keeping up with your exercise, you might be missing out. It turns out that regular physical exercise can boost your memory, focus and reasoning skills. One study even found that Scottish teenagers who got 60 minutes of exercise a day scored a whole grade higher on national exams.

Physical exercise has been linked to a number of positive changes inside our brains. Regular aerobic exercise appears to be linked with an enlarged hippocampus. That's the area of the brain linked to learning and memory. Other studies have suggested that exercise four hours after learning allows new information to be better integrated into our memories. Looking inside our brains, it seems that exercise triggers tiny bursts of electrical energy, known as 'brain ripples' which are thought to be connected to the process of storing and organising memories. Exercise could also lead to improved executive function. This is the part of our brain that's responsible for things including working memory and self-control. A recent study showed that students who carried out ten minutes of moderate exercise showed improved cognitive performance afterwards.

As well as the direct physical benefits of exercise on our brains, there are other associated advantages. Exercise leads to the release of endorphins. These chemicals help to alleviate the effects of stress and can improve our mood. Exam preparation can be both a cause of stress and something that's adversely affected by it. Exercise reduces your stress so that you can focus on your revision. Good sleep habits are also important for brain health and function. And this is another area where exercise helps out. Regular exercise has been shown to lead to better sleep and fewer episodes of insomnia. A study from the University of Texas also linked it to longer instances of deep sleep. When you're asleep, your body processes memories, so it's another way that exercise can take you to higher grades.

Exercise benefits both our mental and physical health and has clear benefits for academic performance. So, while it's important to spend time studying, don't forget to keep some time back for physical activity.
chineseParagraphs: 考试季让你埋头苦读，不去健身房了吗？学习固然重要，但如果不坚持锻炼，你可能会错失良机。事实证明，规律的体育锻炼可以提高你的记忆力、注意力和推理能力。一项研究甚至发现，每天锻炼60分钟的苏格兰青少年在全国考试中成绩整整高出一个等级。

体育锻炼与大脑内部的许多积极变化有关。规律的有氧运动似乎与海马体的增大有关。那是大脑中与学习和记忆相关的区域。其他研究表明，学习后四小时进行锻炼有助于新信息更好地被整合到我们的记忆中。观察我们的大脑内部，运动似乎会触发微小的电能量爆发，称为“脑波涟漪”，被认为与存储和组织记忆的过程有关。运动也可能改善执行功能。这是我们大脑中负责工作记忆和自我控制等功能的区域。最近的一项研究表明，进行十分钟适度运动的学生随后表现出认知能力的提升。

除了运动对大脑的直接身体益处外，还有其他相关优势。运动导致内啡肽的释放。这些化学物质有助于减轻压力的影响，并能改善我们的情绪。备考既是压力的来源，也会受到压力的不利影响。运动可以减轻你的压力，让你能专注于复习。良好的睡眠习惯对大脑健康和功能也很重要。这是运动能提供帮助的另一个领域。规律的运动已被证明可以改善睡眠，减少失眠。德克萨斯大学的一项研究还将其与更长的深度睡眠时间联系起来。当你睡觉时，你的身体会处理记忆，所以这是运动能帮你取得更好成绩的另一种方式。
运动有益于我们的身心健康，对学业成绩也有明显的好处。因此，虽然花时间学习很重要，但别忘了留出一些时间进行体育活动。

vocabulary.definition: 刻苦学习，用功读书（口语，固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: hit the books /ˌhɪt ðə ˈbʊks/ phr. 刻苦学习，用功读书（口语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: I need to hit the books if I want to pass the exam.
vocabulary.translation: 如果我想通过考试，就需要用功读书。

vocabulary.definition: 跟上，与……保持同步（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: keeping up with /ˌkiːpɪŋ ˈʌp wɪð/ phr. 跟上，与……保持同步（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: It's hard to keep up with all the latest developments in technology.
vocabulary.translation: 跟上所有最新的技术发展很难。

vocabulary.definition: 错过（机会或好处）（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: missing out /ˌmɪsɪŋ ˈaʊt/ phr. 错过（机会或好处）（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Don't miss out on the opportunity to study abroad.
vocabulary.translation: 不要错过出国留学的机会。

vocabulary.entry: aerobic exercise /eəˈrəʊbɪk ˈeksəsaɪz/ n. 有氧运动（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Swimming is a good form of aerobic exercise.
vocabulary.translation: 游泳是一种很好的有氧运动。

vocabulary.entry: enlarged /ɪnˈlɑːdʒd/ adj. 增大的，扩大的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The doctor noticed an enlarged heart on the X-ray.
vocabulary.translation: 医生在X光片上注意到心脏增大了。

vocabulary.definition: 海马体（神经解剖学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: hippocampus /ˌhɪpəˈkæmpəs/ n. 海马体（神经解剖学术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The hippocampus plays a crucial role in forming new memories.
vocabulary.translation: 海马体在形成新记忆方面起着关键作用。

vocabulary.entry: integrate /ˈɪntɪɡreɪt/ v. 使结合，使整合（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The school aims to integrate technology into all subjects.
vocabulary.translation: 该校旨在将技术融入所有学科。

vocabulary.entry: trigger /ˈtrɪɡə(r)/ v. 触发，引发（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Certain foods can trigger a migraine headache.
vocabulary.translation: 某些食物可能引发偏头痛。

vocabulary.definition: 脑波涟漪（神经科学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: brain ripple /ˈbreɪn ˌrɪpl/ n. 脑波涟漪（神经科学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Brain ripples are believed to play a role in memory consolidation.
vocabulary.translation: 脑波涟漪被认为在记忆巩固中发挥作用。

vocabulary.definition: 执行功能（心理学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: executive function /ɪɡˈzekjətɪv ˈfʌŋkʃn/ n. 执行功能（心理学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Executive function includes skills like planning and self-control.
vocabulary.translation: 执行功能包括计划和控制等技能。

vocabulary.definition: 工作记忆（心理学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: working memory /ˈwɜːkɪŋ ˈmeməri/ n. 工作记忆（心理学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Working memory allows us to hold information temporarily.
vocabulary.translation: 工作记忆让我们能够暂时保存信息。

vocabulary.entry: self-control /ˌself kənˈtrəʊl/ n. 自我控制（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Self-control is an important skill for success.
vocabulary.translation: 自我控制是成功的重要技能。

vocabulary.entry: moderate /ˈmɒdərət/ adj. 适度的，中等的
vocabulary.example: Regular moderate exercise is good for your health.
vocabulary.translation: 定期适度运动对健康有益。

vocabulary.entry: cognitive performance /ˈkɒɡnətɪv pəˈfɔːməns/ n. 认知表现（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The study measured cognitive performance in elderly adults.
vocabulary.translation: 这项研究测量了老年人的认知表现。

vocabulary.definition: 内啡肽（生物化学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: endorphin /enˈdɔːfɪn/ n. 内啡肽（生物化学专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Exercise releases endorphins that make you feel good.
vocabulary.translation: 运动释放内啡肽，让你感觉良好。

vocabulary.entry: alleviate /əˈliːvieɪt/ v. 减轻，缓解（书面语）
vocabulary.example: This medicine should alleviate your symptoms.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药应该能缓解你的症状。

vocabulary.entry: adversely /ˈædvɜːsli/ adv. 不利地，有害地（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The decision affected her adversely.
vocabulary.translation: 这个决定对她产生了不利影响。

vocabulary.entry: revision /rɪˈvɪʒn/ n. 复习，修订（英式）
vocabulary.example: The exam is next week, so I need to start my revision.
vocabulary.translation: 考试在下周，所以我需要开始复习了。

vocabulary.definition: 失眠（症）（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: insomnia /ɪnˈsɒmniə/ n. 失眠（症）（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: He has suffered from insomnia for many years.
vocabulary.translation: 他患失眠症多年。

vocabulary.definition: 深度睡眠（睡眠学专业术语）
vocabulary.entry: deep sleep /ˈdiːp sliːp/ n. 深度睡眠（睡眠学专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Deep sleep is important for physical recovery.
vocabulary.translation: 深度睡眠对身体恢复很重要。

vocabulary.entry: academic performance /ˌækəˈdemɪk pəˈfɔːməns/ n. 学业成绩（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Good nutrition is linked to better academic performance.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的营养与更好的学业成绩有关。
